chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Willy Lewis's band: Herman Chittison, Bill Coleman and singing rehearsals
summary: Pianist Herman Chittison, Bill Coleman's absence, and a first month of singing rehearsals of German and French songs under leader Willy Lewis, who advised him to sing like Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So we had a boy on piano, his name was Chitterson, Herman Chitterson (PHONETIC), he was beautiful. He had that Chopin touch, Beautiful. And by the way, there was a boy named Bill Coleman, we were always in bands together. Me and him were playing (Cecil Scott) out of Cincinnati.

Cecil Scott. And we always worked beside each other on many things, many gigs. So I knew him. I knew him. So when I got there, well, he was in India. So I played first trumpet part, they had a boy named Hamilton but I think he was from Martinique or Guadeloupe somewhere. But they weren't all Americans (inaudible).

So the first month was rehearsing. I'd rehearse -- voice rehearsal. We were singing, we were singing German songs, in choir, French songs in the choir. And then you had to get your solos together, too, because that band would get out there and just put on a show and be there for an hour singing. And then the leader, Willy Lewis, would feel good and say, "Go home everybody but the pianist," because he'd

want to make that money. And I realized singing/ And these guys, all of them had big -- was going to school, studying modern theory and composition and conducting. I said, 'What?' They were going to school. I said, I'm going to school, too,

First I asked him, I said -- the leader, I said, what should I do? He said, 'Man, sing like Louis Armstrong.' See, I didn't appreciate that. I was angry with him. And I said, you're trying to fool me. I don't like that. Keep that in mind. He said, well, I was only kidding. I said, yeah, me, too.
